description: FrEDI is the US Environmental Protection Agency's R model for estimating annual physical and economic impacts of temperature change. Its sector modules include roads, rail, urban drainage, coastal properties and electricity transmission and distribution, alongside health, agriculture and other impacts. Users supply temperature and socioeconomic scenarios; outputs are sector and geographic impact estimates by year for the contiguous United States and District of Columbia. The repository describes projections through the twenty-first century with an optional extension to 2300. Source code remains free under MIT-style EPA terms and the repository retains previously published technical material. A 2025 EPA notice says the agency removed the former dissemination page and now keeps this repository as an archive of peer-reviewed work, following an information-quality correction request closed in 2026. This status is a limitation: users should check version and correction context before relying on impact estimates. FrEDI is an impact emulator, not a physical road or power-grid simulator. It serves climate-risk scenario comparison for infrastructure. The catalogue's model-diva-coastal-impact-adaptation is a separate coastal-impact model for comparison; no common scenario was run. No dataset was downloaded.
